meta: You ask AI for three good books. It answers fast and sounds sure, but one of them doesn't exist. This is called AI hallucination. Here's why it happens and how to cut it down.
prompt: If you're not sure, say you don't know. Give me sources so I can check.

muc.title: The book that doesn't exist
muc.text: You ask AI for three good books. It answers right away, very sure of itself. You look them up, and one of them doesn't exist.

muc.title: This has a real name
muc.text: This is called AI hallucination: a wrong answer that sounds true.

muc.title: Why does it make things up?
muc.text: Remember the last video: AI guesses the next word that sounds most likely. When it doesn't know, it doesn't stop. It still guesses a name that sounds very real.

muc.title: Where it happens most
muc.text: It happens most with numbers, book titles, laws and links.

muc.title: Let AI say "I don't know"
muc.text: One way to cut it down: add "if you're not sure, say you don't know".

muc.title: Ask for sources, then check
muc.text: And ask for sources. Click them and check. If a link doesn't open, don't trust it.

muc.title: Add these two sentences
muc.text: Next time you ask for numbers or important facts, add those two sentences. AI is a great assistant, but you're the one who checks in the end.
